A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MERA and retain the same core experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching content moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-modality continual-learning experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and stagewise raw results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds EProj comparisons, MCUB-4 evaluation, and noisy-replay experiments.

M1.justification: The core weighted merging and connector-only realignment procedure is unchanged. Appendix A.3 newly proposes adaptations using final encoder layers or embedding layers for architectures without separate connectors or encoders. These procedural extensions are proposed without experimental evaluation.

E1.justification: The original eight captioning and QA datasets remain. v2 adds MCUB-4, requiring simultaneous inference over image, video, audio, and point cloud, substantially extending coverage beyond separate modality tasks. Appendix A.5 also introduces corrupted replay-pair conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds EProj, which freezes the LLM and trains modality-specific components, to the existing backward/forward comparisons, Table 2, and raw-result tables. Fine-Tuning, Replay, EWC, and PathWeave remain; PathWeave's adaptation details are relocated rather than changed.

E3.justification: Existing splits, model configuration, training hyperparameters, and metrics remain unchanged. Added protocols evaluate MCUB-4 accuracy after all four learning stages, corrupt 10% or 50% of replay pairs, and exempt EProj from the initial 100% relative-gain convention. The noise experiment's replay fraction is unclear: Table 7 specifies 10%, but its clean row matches the 1% results.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 and Table 7 add a focused robustness test examining sensitivity to mismatched text-modality replay pairs. The component ablation and realignment-across-methods results in Tables 4 and 5 are unchanged, while existing transfer analyses are reorganized.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly state that experimental results come from single runs. The existing practice of reporting means and standard deviations across learning stages remains; v2 adds no repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained raw scores match exactly between v1 Tables 9-10 and v2 Tables 11-12, but v2 adds EProj, MCUB-4, and noisy-replay results. EProj's final backward relative gain of 87.75% reduces MERA's reported margin from 20.37 to 12.09 percentage points without changing MERA's 99.84%. New MCUB-4 results also distinguish the replay variants: MERA (10%) leads sequentially at 72.70, while MERA (1%) leads in reverse order at 61.22.

T1.justification: The merging rule, relative-gain definitions, and EWC equations remain mathematically equivalent. v2's feature-distribution notation and explicit realignment objective restate the existing mechanism and training description; they introduce no substantive new derivation, proof, or formal result.

C1.justification: Both versions identify forgetting and misalignment, propose MERA to address them, and claim nearly lossless four-modality retention. v2's state-of-the-art wording and description of 99.84% as an average refine the presentation of retained claims rather than redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A substantially expands interpretation: it distinguishes distribution-shift misalignment from broader forgetting, proposes an imbalance explanation for replay's misalignment, and interprets training-order effects through curriculum learning. It also discusses architectural applicability and noisy-replay robustness. The limitations now explicitly identify the LLaVA-like architecture restriction, replacing the earlier two-task limitation.

D1.justification: v2 documents replay corruption through text-modality mispairing and explicitly states in Appendix C.3 that baselines share the common training hyperparameters. Existing encoder choices, LoRA settings, hardware, dataset filtering, and GPT-4o mini evaluation prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises research positioning: it adds merging-based continual learning as a category and replaces the model-merging subsection with a discussion of continual learning for MLLMs. Numerous added works support distinctions between vision-language-only methods and PathWeave's modality-incremental setting.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method explanation are extensively rewritten. Preliminary definitions move into Section 3, plasticity evaluation joins the main results, transfer and misalignment analyses form a Discussions section, and efficiency moves to the appendix. The technical appendices are also consolidated and reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds a four-panel misalignment illustration, annotates the existing pipeline with alignment states, and introduces MCUB-4 and noise-result tables. Existing plots gain EProj curves and revised legends, the forward-gain axis expands, and the efficiency table moves to the appendix. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: EProj and MCUB-4 strengthen the empirical comparison and test simultaneous multimodal use, while the new diagram and discussion clarify realignment. These gains are partly offset by new reporting problems: Table 7 specifies 10% replay although its clean row matches the 1% results, and the prose beside Table 2 reverses the sequential/reverse stability rankings. Overall, the additions support a limited net improvement.
